title: Show attempt phase and delivery evidence in JetBrains task detail
description:
Objective: let a human see the evidence the new rules act on. Without a surface, a refused approval or a withheld dependent claim looks like an unexplained failure.

Deliverable: the JetBrains task detail panel gains a read-only Delivery block listing the current candidate's short sha and base, the latest check run's command and exit code, the delivery receipt's target and landed revision, and the owning attempt's phase. The plugin Task model in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt gains the matching nullable fields, and a task with none of them renders exactly as it does today.

Not in scope: the full Delivery and Attention dashboard redesign, which belongs to Wave 2, board card badges, and VS Code parity. This is a minimal read-only block inside the existing detail panel, sized so the pilot is observable.

Verification: cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test.
definitionOfDone: The JetBrains Task model parses the current candidate, latest check run, delivery receipt and attempt phase, with a MoeJsonTest case covering a fully populated payload
Task detail renders a Delivery block showing candidate sha and base, check command and exit code, receipt target and landed revision, and attempt phase
A task carrying none of those fields renders exactly as it does today, proven by a test
The rendering helper is a pure headless-testable function so JUnit asserts it without an IDE fixture
cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test is green
taskRails: Read-only surface: no new action buttons and no approval flow changes.
Wave 2 owns the Delivery and Attention dashboard; do not build it here.
VS Code parity is a follow-up card, not part of this task.

implementationPlan.description: CONFIRM THE DATA GAP THIS CARD ASSUMES AWAY, THEN READ THE SEAMS. Read-only, no edits. The card's deliverable says the plugin Task model 'gains the matching nullable fields', which reads as though the daemon already sends them. It does not, and that is the single most important fact for this task. Verify it yourself rather than trusting this note. (a) grep packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts for currentCandidate, latestCheckRun, deliveryReceipt and attemptPhase: zero hits. Candidate, CheckRun, DeliveryReceipt and ExecutionAttempt are SEPARATE records under .moe/candidates, .moe/checks, .moe/receipts and .moe/attempts, keyed by candidateId or taskId. They are not fields on Task. (b) Read StateManager.getSnapshot around line 1171: it serves project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels and decisions. The four delivery collections are absent, so the board socket never carries them. (c) Read WebSocketServer.sendStateSnapshot around line 285 and broadcast just above it: the plugin's whole view of a task is the raw persisted Task record from that snapshot plus TASK_UPDATED events. (d) Confirm the plugin has no way to ask for more: grep MoeCommandSender for sendMessage and note there is no per-task detail request, only mutations plus GET_CHANNELS, GET_MESSAGES and GET_PINS. (e) Note that get_context DOES already project currentCandidate (getContext.ts around line 287) but that is the MCP path for agents, not the plugin's WebSocket path. Write all of this into the step note. Conclusion to carry into step 2: this card cannot be delivered as a client-only change, and the scope must grow by one daemon-side projection. If any of the above turns out to be false because a sibling landed it meanwhile, say so and drop step 2.
implementationPlan.note: Read-only confirmation: schema has zero currentCandidate/latestCheckRun/deliveryReceipt/attemptPhase hits; StateManager stores four separate maps and getSnapshot omits all. WebSocketServer broadcasts raw events and snapshot tasks. getContext selects last listCandidatesForTask result by createdAt/id, MCP only. MoeCommandSender has no task-detail query (plan's read-message list is incomplete: also GET_DECISIONS/ACTIVITY_LOG/METRICS, none fetch evidence). Thus step 2 serving-only projection is necessary approved scope growth, without altering getSnapshot/persistence. Receipt prerequisite is in git history (11b6216/81bdc8a/792b02c). Task baseline exists (13:47Z); shared foreign dirty paths preserved, including staged WebSocketServer and unrelated qaApprove.ts UU. No edits or tests in this exploration step.

implementationPlan.description: PROJECT THE EVIDENCE ONTO THE TASK THE BOARD IS SENT. Add a derived delivery projection in the daemon, and keep it strictly a SERVING concern: it is computed when a task is sent to a plugin client, never persisted onto the Task record and never written to disk. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.ts exporting one pure function that takes the state handle and a task and returns either undefined or a small object carrying the current candidate's id, short sha and base revision, the latest check run's command and exit code, the delivery receipt's target and landed revision, and the owning attempt's phase. Resolve each from the existing stores rather than re-reading disk, reusing their established selection rules: the candidate is the task's current one by createdAt then id, exactly as getContext.ts already selects it, and the check run and receipt hang off THAT candidate, not off the task, because a check or receipt belongs to a frozen candidate. Return undefined when the task has none of them, so a project that has never recorded delivery evidence produces byte-identical payloads to today, which is the third Definition-of-Done item and the compatibility guarantee for every existing client. Error handling: a missing or malformed record is treated as absent rather than throwing, because this runs inside snapshot serving on every board connect and one corrupt file must not take the socket down; log at debug and carry on. Then apply it in exactly two places in WebSocketServer.ts: sendStateSnapshot, mapping the filtered task list, and the TASK_UPDATED path in broadcast, so a live update carries the same shape as the initial snapshot. Do not touch getSnapshot itself, which other callers use and which must keep returning persisted records.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented derived Task.delivery at snapshot serving and TASK_UPDATED only; raw getSnapshot/persisted tasks unchanged. Reuses candidate/check ordering, candidate-keyed receipt lookup (ambiguous omitted), candidate owning attempt or current pre-candidate attempt. Guards malformed records and debug logs failures. Full sha is retained alongside shortSha for copying. Tests advanced from step 5 to establish red first: scratch no-evidence stub 10 failed/1 passed -> real implementation 11 passed; repo focused gate now 14/14 including actual WebSocket snapshot/update/no-evidence byte-equality/archived/corrupt cases. Existing client GET_STATE auto-refresh every 3000ms covers evidence-only writes without store event changes. Baseline full daemon: exit1, 1399 tests pass, 29 files fail loading foreign qaApprove.ts merge markers. Unrelated staged hunks untouched.

implementationPlan.description: PARSE IT IN THE JETBRAINS CLIENT. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt add a nullable delivery holder to Task plus the small data classes it needs, all with defaulted nullable members so every existing construction site and fixture keeps compiling. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt map it in BOTH Task construction sites, the private parseTasks used by parseState and the public parseTask used for single-task messages. Forgetting the second one is the classic miss in that file and the reason a snapshot can look right while a live update silently drops the data. Parse defensively, matching what the blocker-metadata work established there: a missing, null or wrong-shaped delivery object yields null rather than throwing; each scalar is read only after a kind guard so a number never becomes an id string; the exit code is read as an integer and left null when it is not one; and no value is trimmed, normalised or reformatted, because these are identifiers a human will compare against git. Error handling is the point of this step: malformed delivery metadata must never drop the otherwise valid task it rides on, since that would blank a board column over one bad record. Reuse the strict helpers already present rather than the permissive legacy getters.
implementationPlan.note: Added nullable TaskDelivery and candidate/check/receipt data classes with nullable defaults. Both parseTasks and parseTask map delivery; strict strings preserve bytes and signed exit code uses guarded BigDecimal.intValueExact with Int bounds. Bad holder/nested shapes yield null without dropping task. Added 4 tests ahead of step 5. Fresh Gradle codec red: 22 tests/3 failed on old parser (payload missing), green: 22 tests/0 failed, BUILD SUCCESSFUL exit0; test task executed under jetbrains-gradle lease. Exact whitespace/case/command newline preserved; numeric string/Boolean/fraction/overflow/huge-exponent cases covered.

implementationPlan.description: RENDER IT, THROUGH A PURE HELPER THE TESTS CAN DRIVE. The fourth Definition-of-Done item requires the rendering decision to be a pure headless-testable function, so create moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt with no Swing and no IntelliJ imports, and declare its data types at TOP LEVEL rather than inside a companion object, because a classifier nested in a companion is not importable as Outer.Inner and has already cost this repo a failed build. It takes the parsed delivery holder and returns either nothing to show or an ordered list of label and value rows, each label a MoeBundle key rather than a literal string. Rules: show a row only when its value is actually present, so a partially populated task shows a partial block rather than empty labels; abbreviate a sha for display while keeping the full value available, since a reviewer compares the short form by eye and pastes the long one; render an exit code of zero as a pass and any non-zero as a failure, and note in a comment that a check run is what the runner REPORTED, never proof the daemon executed anything, which is the boundary the check-run card established and which this surface must not overstate. Then wire it into TaskDetailDialog.kt as a read-only block: no buttons, no actions, no approval flow changes, which is the first task rail. Reuse the existing single state listener and its disposal rather than adding a subscription, and refresh the block from the updated task so an approval or a landing is reflected without reopening the dialog. Add the message keys to moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties.
implementationPlan.note: Pure headless helper with top-level row/outcome types; seven ordered optional rows, exact full tokens retained with 8-char display, reported exit 0 PASS/nonzero FAIL. Read-only dialog block reuses listener/disposal, hides whole wrapper when absent (no legacy spacing), refreshes only delivery content, and uses literal noneditable text areas with selectable full revision (no action/button). Added nine bundle keys. Test-first helper skeleton produced 7 tests/6 failures; implemented helper + dialog: fresh Gradle focused run BUILD SUCCESSFUL exit0, MoeJsonTest 22 + DeliveryPresentationTest 7 =29 green. Exhaustive 128 partial combinations, empty/null, exact strings, signed exits, full/short SHA, literal markup, bundle coverage.

implementationPlan.description: TEST BOTH LAYERS, NAMING EVERY CASE. Daemon side, in a new packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.test.ts using ToolTestHarness: a task with a candidate, a check and a receipt projects all of them; the candidate chosen is the current one when several exist; a check and receipt belonging to an OLDER candidate are not shown against a newer one; a task with no evidence projects undefined and its served payload is byte-identical to the unprojected record; a corrupt or missing record is treated as absent rather than throwing; and the attempt phase reflects the owning attempt. Plugin side, in moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJsonTest.kt: a fully populated payload round-trips through BOTH parseState and parseTask with every value byte-exact, which is the first Definition-of-Done item; absent, null and wrong-typed delivery objects each yield null without dropping the task; and a numeric field arriving as a string does not become an id. New moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentationTest.kt, plain JUnit 4 in the MetricsPanelTest style: every row present renders in order; each partially populated combination renders only its own rows; nothing to show when empty, which pins the render-as-today guarantee; exit code zero versus non-zero; sha abbreviation keeps the full value; and a key-coverage check that loads the bundle from the test classpath and asserts every key the helper can emit is defined, so a missing localisation fails the build rather than shipping a raw placeholder. Assert exact strings and exact enum values throughout, never truthiness.
implementationPlan.note: All planned cases are present (tests were advanced into implementation steps for red-first). Daemon 17/17 green: full projection, current candidate timestamp/id, older-candidate exclusion, latest check/legacy dates, owning/pre-candidate/missing/wrong-task attempt, malformed/null/ambiguous records, byte-identical raw+served legacy payload, no writes/mutation, actual WebSocket snapshot/update/direct-edit paths, archive filtering, and forged metadata refusal. Discovered plan gap: seven direct TASK_UPDATED replies were raw (would erase projected evidence); added shared serving helper for them and delivery to UPDATE_TASK denylist. Scratch tests first proved both defects (15 pass/2 fail), repo now17 green. Same owned server file, no new scope category. Plugin re-run fresh with --rerun-tasks BUILD SUCCESSFUL exit0, 29 tests/0 failures (22 codec +7 presentation), all 11 Gradle tasks executed.

implementationPlan.description: MUTATION RED, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, HAND OFF. (a) These are new files, so establish the red by mutation, in a scratch copy and never in the shared checkout peers are working in, restoring after each and re-verifying with a separate status call. Perform at least four and name the failing test for each: make the projection return an object instead of undefined when there is no evidence, which must break the renders-as-today case; drop the parseTask mapping and keep only parseTasks, which must break the single-task round-trip and is the classic miss in that file; resolve the check and receipt from the task instead of from the current candidate, which must break the older-candidate case; and treat a non-zero exit code as a pass, which must break the exit-code case. A mutation that breaks nothing means that behaviour has no test. (b) Gates: the card names cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test, so run it and require BUILD SUCCESSFUL with nonzero JUnit counts. Because step 2 touches the daemon, also run the daemon suite from the repository root with npm.cmd on Windows and require exit 0 with a count no lower than before, plus npx tsc --noEmit. Acquire the shared Gradle slot through the Moe resource protocol before the plugin leg and release it either way; never cancel a peer's build or delete a shared cache, and treat an UP-TO-DATE Gradle result as no test run. Set GRADLE_OPTS to raise the client heap if the Gradle daemon reports an out-of-memory during cleanup on this box. (c) Adversarially review: is the projection genuinely serving-only, with nothing persisted onto a Task record or written to disk; does a project with no delivery evidence produce byte-identical payloads; are both parser paths mapped; can malformed metadata drop a task or take down the snapshot; does the detail block add any action, which a task rail forbids; is the dashboard left to Wave 2; and did anything VS Code change, which is explicitly a follow-up card. (d) Complete through moe.complete_task with the commands, exit codes, counts and mutation results, listing every modified path. State plainly in the summary that the card assumed the plugin could already see this evidence, that it could not, and that the daemon projection in step 2 is the added scope that made the rest possible, so a reviewer can judge that expansion on the record.

comments.author: architect-8b93cc67
comments.content:
SCOPE EXPANSION, stated up front so a reviewer judges it on the record rather than discovering it in a diff.

This card assumes the plugin can already see delivery evidence and needs only to render it. It cannot. I verified this against merged main (cf20174) before planning:

- Candidate, CheckRun, DeliveryReceipt and ExecutionAttempt are four SEPARATE record types under .moe/, keyed by candidateId or taskId. None is a field on Task. Grepping schema.ts for currentCandidate, latestCheckRun, deliveryReceipt or attemptPhase returns nothing.
- StateManager.getSnapshot (line 1171) serves project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels and decisions. The four delivery collections are absent, so the board socket never carries them.
- The plugin's whole view of a task is that raw persisted record, from the snapshot plus TASK_UPDATED.
- There is no per-task detail request to fetch more with: MoeCommandSender's only read messages are GET_CHANNELS, GET_MESSAGES and GET_PINS.
- get_context DOES project currentCandidate (getContext.ts:287), but that is the MCP path agents use, not the plugin's WebSocket path.

So a client-only change cannot satisfy a single Definition-of-Done item. The plan adds ONE daemon file, a serving-side projection applied in exactly two places in WebSocketServer, and that is the only scope beyond the card. Nothing is persisted onto a Task record and getSnapshot itself is untouched, because the evidence is derived from four other records and a stored copy would be a second source of truth that can go stale. That also keeps the epic's additive, migration-free rail intact.

That expansion is why the plan reports ten files and trips the size warning. Seven of them are the card's own surface plus tests; three are the projection and its test. I did not split the card, because a JetBrains surface with no data behind it is not shippable in halves.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION POINTS worth reading before starting, both of which have bitten this repo already:

1. The check run and the receipt hang off a frozen CANDIDATE, not off the task. Resolve them through the task's current candidate or the panel will show a check result from superseded bytes, which is exactly the class of lie Wave 1 exists to end. One of the required mutations targets this.

2. MoeJson has TWO Task construction sites, parseTasks for snapshots and parseTask for single-task messages. Mapping only the first makes a snapshot look correct while every live update silently drops the data. Same trap recorded during the blocker-metadata work in the same file.

Rails respected: read-only block with no actions, no Wave 2 dashboard, no VS Code. VS Code parity remains a follow-up card and should be filed once this lands, since the projection will already be serving the data it needs.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Adding the four collections to the snapshot as sibling arrays and joining them client-side - rejected: it matches how workers and channels are served, but it pushes the current-candidate selection rule into Kotlin where it would drift from the daemon's own, and the card explicitly wants the Task model to carry the fields. Persisting the derived fields onto the Task record - rejected outright: they are derived from four other records, persisting them would create a second source of truth that can go stale, and an epic rail keeps the store additive and migration-free. Adding a per-task detail request to the plugin protocol - rejected as heavier than the card warrants and a new round trip for data the snapshot can carry. Rendering inside TaskDetailDialog without a pure helper - rejected by the fourth Definition-of-Done item and by testability: the board dialog cannot be asserted without an IDE fixture. Blocking the card until someone else adds the projection - considered, and rejected because no sibling owns it: the remaining Wave 1 rows are the wrapper receipt work and the integration pass, so blocking would strand this surface indefinitely. The honest move is to expand scope by one file and say so in the completion summary.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured on merged main (cf20174). The card contains one wrong assumption that decides the whole shape of the work: its deliverable reads as though the plugin already receives candidate, check, receipt and attempt data and merely needs to render it. It does not. Those are four separate record types under .moe/, keyed by candidateId or taskId, and none of them is a field on Task. The board socket sends exactly what getSnapshot builds - project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels, decisions - so the plugin's entire view of a task is the raw persisted record. There is also no per-task detail request in MoeCommandSender to fetch more with; the only read messages are GET_CHANNELS, GET_MESSAGES and GET_PINS. get_context does already project currentCandidate, but that is the MCP path agents use, not the plugin's WebSocket path. So a client-only change cannot satisfy a single Definition-of-Done item, and the scope has to grow by one daemon-side serving projection. Two details make that projection non-obvious: the check run and the receipt belong to a frozen CANDIDATE rather than to the task, so they must be resolved through the task's current candidate or a stale check will be shown against new bytes; and the projection must return nothing at all when there is no evidence, because that is what keeps existing payloads byte-identical.
planningNotes.risks: Seven files is above the five-file target, and the reason is the scope expansion in step 2 rather than drift - the worker should say so rather than let a reviewer read it as creep. The likeliest wrong implementation is resolving the check run and receipt from the task instead of from its current candidate, which would show evidence from superseded bytes, and one of the required mutations targets exactly that. The second is mapping only parseTasks and not parseTask, so snapshots look right while live updates silently drop the data; that trap is already recorded from the blocker-metadata work in the same file. Keep the projection serving-only: nothing persisted, nothing written, and getSnapshot itself untouched since other callers depend on it. A project with no delivery evidence must produce byte-identical payloads, which is both the compatibility guarantee and a Definition-of-Done item. Do not overstate what a check run proves - it is runner-reported, not daemon-executed. Respect the rails: no actions in the block, no Wave 2 dashboard, no VS Code. On this box a Gradle run can report an out-of-memory in its cleanup thread when the temp directory is large, which is cosmetic after BUILD SUCCESSFUL but worth raising the client heap for, and the shared Gradle slot must be serialised through the resource protocol.
